question: Who was the Solicitor General of India in 2024, who was re-appointed in 2023?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Tushar Mehta**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Tushar Mehta** was reappointed as the Solicitor General of India for a term of three years in **2023**. He continued in this role in **2024**, making him the incumbent Solicitor General during that year. 
• The Solicitor General is the second-highest law officer in India, assisting the Attorney General in legal matters related to the government. 
• **Tushar Mehta** has been serving as Solicitor General of India since **October 2018**. His tenure has been marked by handling several high-profile cases. 
• The Solicitor General is appointed by the **President of India** on the advice of the Union Cabinet. The appointment is typically for a term of three years. 
• Mehta has represented the Union Government in various cases concerning constitutional, civil, and criminal matters, including landmark hearings in the Supreme Court. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Solicitor General of India:** 
• The Solicitor General is responsible for advising the government on legal matters and representing it in courts, particularly in the Supreme Court. 
• The position is a statutory one, but not explicitly mentioned in the **Indian Constitution**. It is governed by statutory rules under the Law Officers (Conditions of Service) Rules, **1987**. 
• The Solicitor General assists the **Attorney General of India**, who is the highest law officer of the country. 
• The office of the Solicitor General is supported by several **Additional Solicitors General**, who also represent the Union Government in various courts. 
• **Role and Functions:** 
• The Solicitor General does not have independent executive authority and works under the direction of the Attorney General. 
• They provide advice on legal issues and appear on behalf of the government in high-profile cases. 
• Prominent cases handled by the Solicitor General include disputes involving constitutional law, taxation, and criminal law. 
• **Historical Context:** 
• Previous Solicitor Generals have included eminent legal personalities like **K.K. Venugopal**, **Mukul Rohatgi**, and **Ranjit Kumar**. 
• The position is considered prestigious and crucial in maintaining the legal framework of the government. 
• **Important Developments:** 
• **Tushar Mehta** has represented the government in cases like the **abrogation of Article 370**, the **Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA)**, and various economic and criminal matters. 
• His tenure has been extended multiple times, reflecting the confidence of the government in his legal expertise. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Appointment Process:** 
• The Solicitor General is appointed by the **President of India** on the recommendation of the **Union Cabinet**. 
• The term of appointment is typically three years, but extensions are possible based on performance and the government’s discretion. 
• **Eligibility and Qualifications:** 
• The Solicitor General is typically an eminent lawyer with extensive experience in constitutional and civil law. 
• They must possess a strong understanding of judicial processes and have a proven track record in handling complex legal cases. 
• **Difference from Attorney General:** 
• While the Attorney General is the chief legal advisor to the government and represents it in crucial cases, the Solicitor General assists in these responsibilities and handles specific cases as directed. 
• The Solicitor General does not directly advise the government but focuses on litigation and courtroom representation.
